text:
samir: Heads-up — I'm opening a PR to split module `networking/v2` into `core` + `cloud-provider`. It moves some outputs and adjusts provider blocks. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4123. Need a quick sanity check on provider pinning, lockfile regen, and any secret path fallout before I merge.

lia: taking a look now. Do you intend to hoist providers to the root or keep them localized to each module? Hoisting changes lockfile behavior.

samir: keeping provider configs local inside the new provider shim module for now, but the PR also adds a root-level providers.tf to unify constraints. Example provider block in the PR:

```
provider "aws" {
  version = "~> 4.60"
  region  = var.region
}
```

I already ran:
```
terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64
```
and included the lockfile update in the PR.

chen: fyi if you add a root providers.tf we need to update CI to init with the root lockfile. CI currently runs `terraform init` per-module; switch to `-chdir=./` or adjust pipeline. Also double-check provider checksums — the lockfile should be committed, not generated in CI.

miguel: quick prod-state note: the module path is changing so the state address will move. Please add a migration plan in the PR description with `terraform state mv` commands. Recommend doing the move during a maintenance window and running a canary (one staging cluster) before global.

carla: small docs nit — update the module README/CHANGELOG and the internal module registry entry. Also bump `module_semver` in the registry metadata so downstream consumers know it's a breaking refactor.

ales: does this touch any k8s manifests? We have the manifest-generator that pulls module outputs (service CIDRs, subnets). If output names change, the generator will break. If you preserved output names we should be fine; otherwise add shims or update the generator.

samir: good call — I preserved most output names but moved a couple under `networking.outputs.vpc_id` -> `networking.core.vpc_id`. I'll add an outputs-compat wrapper in the PR. Also note we changed a Vault secret path: `secret/data/infra/k8s` -> `secret/data/infra/k8s/networking`. That may affect the k8s secret sync job.

lia: I ran `make tf-check` locally and tflint + fmt passed. Lockfile includes provider checksums for both platforms. :+1:

chen: one operational ask — please do not squash the lockfile commit. Keep the lockfile regen as its own commit so we can bisect provider regressions later.

samir: ack — will keep lockfile regen separate. I'll also add the state-move steps and the manifest-generator change. Plan to merge tomorrow 10:00 PST unless there are objections.

infra-bot: Deploy preview (staging) for PR #4123 completed: plan OK, 2 changes to remote state detected. Logs: https://ci.redwood-inference.com/job/4123/plan

infra-sre: noted — we'll monitor the canary and watch for svc/cidr drift alerts. Tagging @eng-oncall for the maintenance window.

miguel: ping me when you're ready to do the state move; I can coordinate the windows and run the commands with you.

samir: thanks all. I added the migration steps + manifest patch in the PR description and marked the lockfile commit as separate. Leaving a note to run `terraform apply -target=module.networking` in staging first.

carla: LGTM once CI uses the root lockfile and the manifest-generator PR lands.

lia: :eyes: will re-run CI checks after any changes.

samir: merging tomorrow unless someone flags anything by EOD. Ping me here for urgent blockers.

chen: reminder — update the infra pipeline to run `terraform init -lockfile=./terraform.lock.hcl` when applying from the repo root.

infra-sre: we'll be on standby during the merge/canary window. Post any alerts in #incidents if you see rollout errors.
